purpose: Isolated root-cause diagnostic for a PT-03-002 stage 4 (draft generation) anomaly: the first core-journey run recorded a client-side timeout waiting for the Draft Generator UI to leave its 'Generating your draft...' state. This diagnostic bypasses the browser UI layer entirely and calls the real, unmodified POST /api/ai/draft route directly (via page.evaluate(fetch(...)) inside an authenticated Playwright browser context, so the request is still same-origin/cookie-authenticated exactly as a real user's would be) to isolate whether the server-side generation itself was slow/broken, or whether the anomaly was UI-layer only.
opportunity_name: Stone Point Credit Income Fund and Stone Point Credit Income Adviser LLC

finding.summary: The real, unmodified /api/ai/draft route returned a genuine HTTP 200 with a full generated grant narrative (31727 bytes) and marked agent_runs.status='completed' (duration_ms=117498, tokens_used=7783 -- a real, successful Claude call, well under the route's own maxDuration=300 budget), but persisted ZERO rows to draft_versions for this organization. The API call itself was never slow or broken -- the original Playwright run's client-side 320s timeout waiting for the UI to leave its 'Generating your draft...' state was very likely this same silent persistence failure surfacing as a stuck client state (the client only advances the wizard on payload.savedVersion truthy paths reachable after a real content response; see code_read_root_cause).

code_read_root_cause.schema_check: information_schema.columns confirms draft_versions.version_number is data_type=integer, is_nullable=NO, column_default=NULL (no default) on this local stack.
code_read_root_cause.trigger_check: pg_trigger for draft_versions (tgrelid='draft_versions'::regclass, not tgisinternal) returned zero rows on this local stack before this diagnostic's fix -- no BEFORE INSERT trigger existed to assign version_number.
code_read_root_cause.migration_source: supabase/migrations/009_draft_versions.sql defines trg_set_draft_version_number (BEFORE INSERT, assigns version_number = MAX(version_number)+1 per opportunity_id via set_draft_version_number()) specifically so 'application code never supplies it (avoids races)' -- migration 009's own header comment. src/lib/drafts/generator.ts's draft_versions insert (~line 966-993) never sets version_number, by design, relying entirely on this trigger.
code_read_root_cause.why_it_silently_swallowed: generator.ts's draft_versions insert is deliberately best-effort: on any insert error (here, a NOT NULL constraint violation on version_number) it only console.error()s 'DRAFT VERSION SAVE ERROR' and leaves savedVersion:null -- it does not throw, so /api/ai/draft's route.ts still returns 200 with the full draftText and confidenceScore regardless of whether the DB write actually succeeded.
code_read_root_cause.client_side_gap: src/app/(dashboard)/draft-generator/page.tsx (~line 950) has a comment reading 'The draft was already auto-saved to draft_versions by the API' and never checks payload.savedVersion for null before calling setDraftText/advancing the wizard via handleGenerateClick -> setStep(4) -- so a savedVersion:null response is visually indistinguishable from a real save.
code_read_root_cause.production_applicability_note: 009_draft_versions.sql is recorded as fully APPLIED in MIGRATION_AUDIT.md's production structural audit (table 193-232, '009_draft_versions.sql' listed under 'Migrations — APPLIED (55 of 112)'), so production's draft_versions table and version_number column almost certainly exist -- but that audit's own stated methodology only confirms CREATE TABLE / ADD COLUMN presence, not trigger objects, so whether production's trg_set_draft_version_number trigger is itself live was NOT independently re-verified by this session. This diagnostic's root cause (missing trigger) is therefore confirmed as a LOCAL-STACK schema gap (same class already found and fixed this session for `programs`/`pipeline_history`, and by a prior session for other tables), not asserted as a current production bug -- but the code-level swallow-and-200 pattern is a real, independent robustness gap regardless of whether the trigger is currently present anywhere: any future drift that breaks it (a migration rollback, a manual DDL change, a differently-provisioned environment, a transient DB error) reproduces total, silent draft loss with zero test coverage and zero user-facing signal.

fix_applied_to_local_stack_only.description: Applied 009_draft_versions.sql's set_draft_version_number() function + trg_set_draft_version_number trigger verbatim to the local stack (idempotent CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION + DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS/CREATE TRIGGER), inside scripts/audit/pt03-002-core-journey.mjs's applyLocalSchemaFixes(), the same local-only mechanism already used this session for the programs/pipeline_history gap. This is a local, non-production DDL change under this script's own control, applied so the rest of the PT-03-002 core journey could be driven and evidenced end to end.
fix_applied_to_local_stack_only.verified_by: scripts/audit/pt03-002-core-journey.mjs's own post-apply check (pg_trigger row count for trg_set_draft_version_number > 0) plus the re-run's stage 4 result recorded in test-evidence/pt-03/core-journey.json.
